title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering
abstract: arXiv:2610.14960v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Can an autonomous AI agent reverse engineer a binary as well as a skilled human analyst? Do they adopt the same strategy, and can agents scale to real-world programs? We compare human and LLM-based software reverse engineering (SRE): nine models tackle two compact static-analysis challenges previously solved by human analysts, scored with a common understanding rubric, and we record their complete interactions with IDA Pro. This lets us compare not only what humans and agents recover, but also how they investigate a binary. The best agents (GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and Kimi K3) achieve statistically human-competitive understanding on both tasks, while weaker models remain far behind. Ablations show that the gap depends on code representation and workflow demands, not on model capability alone: open-weight models improve substantially with richer code representations, whereas frontier models show no significant change. translated_title: 人类与机器：软件逆向工程中AI智能体的比较研究
translated_abstract: 自主AI智能体能否像熟练的人类分析师一样对二进制程序进行逆向工程？它们是否采用相同的策略？智能体能否扩展到真实世界的程序？我们比较了人类与基于大语言模型（LLM）的软件逆向工程（SRE）：九个模型应对两个此前由人类分析师解决的紧凑静态分析挑战，采用统一的理解评分标准进行评分，并记录它们与IDA Pro的完整交互过程。这使我们不仅能比较人类和智能体各自恢复了什么信息，还能比较它们如何对二进制程序进行调查分析。表现最佳的智能体（GPT-5.5 Pro、Claude Opus 4.8和Kimi K3）在两项任务上都达到了与人类具有统计可比性的理解水平，而较弱的模型则远远落后。消融实验表明，这一差距取决于代码表示和工作流程要求，而不仅仅取决于模型能力：开源权重模型在更丰富的代码表示下有显著提升，而前沿模型则没有显著变化。
tldr: 该研究首次系统比较了人类分析师与基于大语言模型的AI智能体在软件逆向工程任务中的表现，发现顶级智能体已达到与人类相当的理解水平，且性能差距主要取决于代码表示和工作流程设计而非模型能力本身。
en_tdlr: This study systematically compares human analysts with LLM-based AI agents on software reverse engineering tasks, finding that top agents achieve human-competitive understanding and that performance gaps depend mainly on code representation and workflow demands rather than model capability alone.
